draft.alt_text: Loan Studio’s dark workspace with sample loan inputs, recent scenarios and a result of 94% estimated approval probability. The inputs are invented examples; the output is a model prediction, not a lender approval.
draft.body:
I’ve rebuilt my loan prediction app with a dark workspace, a clearer result panel and a way to revisit earlier scenarios.

The part I wanted to make easier was comparison. Enter a few example details, see the model’s estimate, then change one input and run it again. You can go back to a recent scenario without filling in the whole form.

The form is now split into three sections: the loan, income and household, and applicant profile. “Load sample” gives you somewhere to start. “New scenario” clears the form when you want to try your own made-up example.

The screenshot shows one of those examples. The model returns a 94% estimated probability of approval for the details entered. That percentage describes the model’s output for this example. It does not tell us the model is 94% accurate, and no lender has approved an application.

The original model is unchanged. Comparison checks returned the same predictions and probabilities after the update. The results card gives the percentage a clear label and shows a few of the submitted inputs, so you can see which example produced it.

One detail matters when comparing runs: changing a field does not change the previous result. You need to select “Run scenario” again. Otherwise, it would be easy to read an old result as though it belonged to the numbers now in the form.

Up to six recent scenarios remain available during the session. They are not saved to a database, and the app does not submit loan applications. Use invented details when trying it.

This is still a portfolio demonstration. I haven’t established that the model is accurate, fair or suitable for real lending. The original project also does not document its currency and amount units, so the values appear without currency symbols.

I want someone exploring the app to be able to follow each result back to the details they entered. The sample, submitted-input summary and recent scenarios give them a way to do that while trying different combinations.

Try Loan Studio with the sample details: https://loan-prediction-app-55ycwzbcqsxtfryemepphw.streamlit.app/
claims: The redesigned interface groups the eleven original inputs and provides sample loading and up to six recent scenarios per session.
The original fitted model is preserved; export validation matched predictions and probabilities for 11,474 examples and numeric boundary cases.
The displayed sample produces a 94% estimated approval probability, not a verified lender approval or model accuracy score.
The app does not submit applications or persist scenarios to a database.
